title: Flow run request
description:
POST /api/bridge/runs.

`idempotencyKey` is REQUIRED and is the deduplication gate: the run row is reserved under a unique constraint on it BEFORE execution begins, so a duplicate returns the existing run instead of executing again. This is load-bearing rather than defensive — triggers fire from retried webhooks, several browser tabs and at-least-once event delivery, so without it 'the customer got three follow-up emails' is a routine outcome. The key must be stable for the same logical event (`binding:<id>:<eventId>`), never a fresh UUID.

protocol.description: Protocol the sender speaks. Receivers reject unknown majors rather than guessing.

flowId.description: Stable flow id. Either this or `graph`, never both.

input.description: Named flow inputs, matching the flow's declared input set.

capabilities.description: Capabilities the flow needs. Checked up front so a flow that would fail halfway — after it has already sent an email — is refused before it starts.

items.description: Dotted capability id. `oaiy.*` is reserved for the platform; products and plugins own their own namespace (`connector.aokie.*`).

mode.description: `sync` waits for the terminal result. `async` returns 202 + runId. `queued` reserves without starting, for a worker to claim.

correlationId.description: Ties this run to one logical interaction (a whole call, not one moment in it).

lineage.description: Set when this run was triggered by another run. The loop guards depend on it, so a dispatcher must populate it.

depth.description: Caps at 16. Terminal flow events can trigger flows, so without a depth cap this is an unbounded fork bomb that presents as a hung machine.
